articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Winter Cleanup Across Bellwood
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in August.
body: The Bellwood Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Celia Caruso, who has lived in Bellwood for 5 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings.
Public works estimates the work will take about 5 weeks once it begins. The plan calls for accessible ramp along Ridge Street, with work expected to start in August.

articles.title: Lydia Donnelly, 78, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Lydia Donnelly for the many years of service to Foundry Row.
body: Born in Foundry Row in the years after the war, Lydia Donnelly spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Mill Hill Lions Club in his or her name.

articles.title: The Kettle Hill Block Association Plans Community Garden for Spring
articles.deck: Residents of Bellwood met on Saturday to talk over the plan.
body: The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.
Several residents on Adams Court said they had been waiting since 1976 for something like this. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at St. Brendan’s hall on Saturday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Council Tables Free Tax Clinic Ordinance
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Keystone Drive disagreed about cost and timing.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Councilmember Simone Nakamura asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500.
Residents of Canal Park said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to the Marsh Landing Pond Committee
body: To the editor: I have lived on Prospect Terrace for 7 years, and I want to say what a difference the Marsh Landing Pond Committee has made. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the December meeting.
Please keep the second recycling drop-off in the budget. Many of us on Prospect Terrace use it every week.
Sergio Schaefer, Eastgate
